On the left bank of the Ishim stands the symbol of the capital – the modern Baiterek monument, 97 metres high. The tower’s observation deck offers a stunning panoramic view of the city. In June 2017, the capital of Kazakhstan gained the status of a city with a population of one million. Its economy is based on trade, transport, communications and construction. Baiterek is the main symbol of Astana and one of the main attractions of Kazakhstan.
One of the largest cities with a populat: Almaty, with a population of more than 1.8 million people, is one of the country’s largest cities and is rightly considered its cultural, financial and economic centre. It lies in the centre of the Eurasian continent, in the south-east of the Republic of Kazakhstan, in the foothills of the Trans-Ili Alatau, the northern range of the Tien Shan. Many tourist routes start from here. In just a few days on a winter trip to Almaty, you can visit snowy mountain peaks and descend into the valley to see the sights of the desert.
In June 2018, Shymkent was also recogniz: In June 2018, Shymkent was also recognised as a city of republican significance. Previously, Shymkent was the administrative centre of the South Kazakhstan (now Turkestan) Region. It is the third-largest city in Kazakhstan by population and the first by area, and is one of the country’s largest industrial, commercial and cultural centres.

Kazakhstan is a secular, multi-confessio: Kazakhstan is a secular, multi-faith country. The most widespread religions are Islam and Christianity.

Kazakh hospitality, which goes back through the centuries, is still very much alive today.
